problem: Caught excluded view-transition and visual PerformanceObserver calls could pass the preceding per-test prototype: realm/native rejection did not reach the native violation journal. Four original tests across both engines reproduced the false acceptance.
change: Record selected view-transition starts and paint-dependent observer acquisition in native Blink before rejection or allowed acquisition. Remove their early realm wrappers so calls reach the authoritative native boundary. Extend strict decoding only for these operations and worker observer identities; caught errors still reject attempt teardown. Shared active/completed/violation accounting remains in use.

applicationRetirementFailure.decision: Keep fail-closed rejection. Completing this gate requires a recorder retirement protocol that prevents losing in-flight records; another passing run cannot erase this observed failure.

legacyRegression.scope: Negative controls intentionally fail original tests. Per-test journal and renderer receipts establish selected recording scope; sampled process custody is not exhaustive.

applications.scope: One application attempt is rejected for an unfinished native write despite normal browser exit; it is not accepted evidence. Remaining original per-test and retry identities, original browser wait, complete native counters and observed group drain verified. The 100ms process sampler is not exhaustive custody or final resource admission. No performance inference.

build.scope: One local incremental build including relink and snapshot generation, not a clean-build benchmark.

limitations: The application gate remains incomplete: one unchanged TodoMVC test passed its body but was rejected during teardown for an unfinished native storage record. Normal browser exit is not sufficient evidence; retain this failure and do not weaken the completion checks.

This closes selected caught view-transition and visual observer recording gaps. It does not complete all painting/capture dependencies: remaining realm guards, implicit behavior, other storage and network exclusions are not admitted.

Worker coverage is a dedicated blob worker selecting a paint observer type. Ordinary Chromium does not deliver window paint entries there; discovery records the attempted dependency, not proof of supported worker paint delivery. Shared/service workers and worklets require separate coverage.
Frame controls exercise a cross-site child and remove it after the native calls. Broader navigation, scope, shutdown and source-location races remain separate.
Strict argument conversion still follows browser binding evaluation; native records precede transition creation/observer registration, not arbitrary user-defined JavaScript argument getters.

Original per-test browser waits, completed counters and observed group drain are verified. Writer PIDs missed by the 100 ms sampler are retained in each result; this is not exhaustive process custody or final resource admission.
The private no-sandbox journal and fresh browser per attempt are correctness prototypes, not production IPC, a new speed result or public runner delivery.

The preceding preparation pipeline screen is separate. No prior painting timings apply automatically to this corrected executable. Representative majority-scenario 2x performance, competitor admission and release remain unfinished.
